name: Datum Calc
tagline: Engineering calculations with real units, as readable maths, with checks and a printable calc sheet.
for: Mechanical, process, structural and electrical engineers, students and lecturers: everyone who writes calculations.
about: Datum Calc is a desktop app for engineering calculation sheets. You type equations with their units, such as Q = 120 m^3/h or P = rho*g*Q*H/eta; Datum Calc shows them as readable maths, works out each answer with its unit, and catches mistakes such as adding metres to seconds on the line where they happen.

Checks compare results with their limits and show PASS or FAIL with the utilisation. The sheet prints as a clean, referenced calc sheet with a title block (project, calc number, by, checked, date, revision) and page numbers, ready to hand in. Ready-made calc packs for pumps, pipes, compressors, heat exchangers, tanks, pipe walls, pipe insulation, vessels, beams, columns, shafts, bolts, welds, thermal expansion, motors, cables and AC circuits start you off. Complex numbers (3 + 4j) work out AC circuits, shown as 3 + 4j or as magnitude and angle.

steps.title: Write the equations
steps.text: Type each equation with its units, top to bottom, as on paper; the maths is shown as you would write it.

steps.title: Check the results
steps.text: Every answer carries its unit; checks against your limits show PASS or FAIL with the utilisation ratio.

steps.title: Print the calc sheet
steps.text: Fill in the title block and print or save a PDF with page numbers and references.

highlights: Equations with real units: about 200 units, SI with prefixes and US customary, absolute and difference temperatures, torques in N·m, dimension errors caught on the line.
Readable maths: what is shown is drawn from the same expression the engine computes.
Checks with PASS or FAIL and the utilisation ratio.
Solve for the value that makes an equation zero within a range, plot functions such as a pump curve against the system curve, and tables with units per column.
Nineteen ready calc packs, each with its reference and a test against a worked example.
Complex numbers for AC circuits: impedances such as (8 + 9.42j) Ω, phasors, complex power, in rectangular or polar form.
Each equation can be shown again with its numbers put in, as on a hand calculation.
A printable calc sheet with a title block, a summary of checks, page numbers and references; inputs and results export as CSV.
